title: Gai Pad Khing – Thai Ginger Chicken Stir-Fry
description: Gai Pad Khing is a classic Thai stir-fry known for its bold ginger aroma, tender chicken, earthy mushrooms, and perfectly balanced savory sauce. Quick-cooked over high heat, this dish combines fresh ginger warmth, umami-rich seasonings, and crisp vegetables for an authentic Thai wok experience.

ingredients.title: For the Chicken & Vegetables
items: Chicken breast or thigh – 300 g, thinly sliced
Fresh ginger – 100 g, julienned into fine matchsticks
Straw mushrooms or oyster mushrooms – 150 g, halved
Red chili (prik chee faa) – 1 small, thinly sliced
Wood ear mushrooms – 1 handful, soaked if dried (optional)

ingredients.title: For the Sauce Mix
items: Dark soy sauce – ½ tsp (for color)
Palm sugar or regular sugar – 1 tsp

ingredients.title: For Aromatics & Cooking
items: Neutral cooking oil – 2 tbsp (rice bran, soybean, or canola)
Freshly ground white pepper – to finish

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Sauce
steps: Combine oyster sauce, light soy sauce, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and chicken stock in a small bowl.
Stir well until the sugar dissolves completely. Set aside.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Heating the Wok
steps: Heat a seasoned wok over high heat until lightly smoking.
Add oil and swirl it around the wok to coat the surface evenly.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Cooking the Aromatics & Chicken
steps: Add chopped garlic and stir-fry for 5–7 seconds until fragrant without browning.
Add sliced chicken and stir-fry quickly until the chicken is about 70% cooked.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Adding Ginger & Vegetables
steps: Add onion, mushrooms, and half of the julienned ginger.
Stir-fry over high heat, allowing the vegetables to develop a light char while maintaining their texture.

instruction.title: Step 5 – Building the Flavor
steps: Pour in the prepared sauce mixture.
Toss everything together until the chicken is fully cooked and the sauce lightly coats all ingredients.

instruction.title: Step 6 – Fresh Ginger Finish
steps: Add the remaining ginger, spring onions, and sliced chili.
Toss briefly for 10–15 seconds to preserve freshness and aroma.

instruction.title: Step 7 – Serving
steps: Transfer immediately to a serving plate.
Finish with freshly ground white pepper and serve hot.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve traditionally with steamed jasmine rice to absorb the savory ginger sauce.
Pair with Thai cucumber salad or a light soup for a balanced meal.
Serve immediately after cooking to enjoy the fresh ginger aroma and wok-fired texture.

chefTips: Slice ginger into thin, even matchsticks rather than chunks for the best texture and flavor release.
Add ginger in two stages — early cooking creates deep warmth, while late addition preserves freshness and spice.
Maintain high heat throughout cooking to achieve authentic Thai wok hei (smoky wok aroma).
Avoid overcrowding the wok, as excess moisture will steam the ingredients instead of stir-frying them.
For extra tender chicken, marinate with a little cornstarch and light soy sauce for 10 minutes before cooking.
Balance the sauce carefully — fish sauce adds saltiness, while sugar rounds out the flavors.
